verdict.rationale: CockroachDB ships its own sandbox-style environments: `cockroach demo` spins up a temporary, in-memory cluster with an optional preloaded dataset, single-node clusters are documented for quick SQL testing, and Cockroach Continuum lets developers and agents deploy virtual clusters on a host cluster. These are separate from production by construction, but the evidence does not document an agent workflow that targets a sandbox rather than production, or explicit guarantees that production data is never touched. missing for 10: documented isolation or guardrails keeping agents (e.g. via the MCP server) off production, a sandbox seeded from production-like data (branching or cloning), and independent or hands-on corroboration of agent sandbox use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: The `cockroach demo` starts a temporary, in-memory CockroachDB cluster of one or more nodes, with or without a preloaded dataset, and opens an interactive SQL shell to the cluster.
A single-node cluster is appropriate for quick SQL testing or app development.
Cockroach Continuum supports cluster virtualization, allowing application developers and agents to deploy virtual clusters on a dedicated host cluster.
